assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single flat raster playing-card back prototype for Design 2, portrait 5:7 proportions, ideally 1500 by 2100 pixels. Reference image 1 is Design 1 and is ONLY a geometry reference: retain its full-card proportions, narrow antique-white outside margin, softly rounded silhouette, border band width and curved inner corners. Replace ALL of its ornament. At nominal 750 by 1050 coordinates the outside decorative rule is approximately x=23 to 727 and y=16 to 1034; the inside edge of the floral frame is approximately x=72 to 678 and y=70 to 980, with rounded inner corners. Full bleed canvas of ONE card, no surrounding scene, no mockup, no labels. Background throughout is flat uniform antique white #FAEBD7, including visible negative space within the field. The perimeter floral band must have its OWN unmistakably Chinese lotus/peony rhythm, narrow winding jointed stems, turned lotus leaves, alternating blossoms and small buds, as decorative porcelain rim or silk border art. No Design 1 acanthus, berry clusters, daisy border, Morris foliage, Mucha flourishes, Safavid cartouche or pointed ogival compartments. Aim for two-way 180-degree rotational symmetry and a centered radial floral medallion, no directional central flower. Detailed ornamental illustration with very fine linework and restrained pigment variation confined to colored shapes; no fake aged paper texture, gradients on the ground, 3D embossing or photographic lighting. No people, animals, landscapes, lettering, Chinese characters, symbols, logos or watermark. Direction A: Ming blue-and-white porcelain meets Tang treasure-flower geometry. Only cobalt and soft variations of cobalt ink on the antique-white ground. Compose a small precise eightfold composite lotus/peony treasure-flower roundel at the exact center, about 28 percent of card width. Surround it with four smaller radial floral roundels placed as a balanced two-by-two pattern, connected by fine Chinese lotus scrolls with sharply articulated petals and small fanlike lobed leaves. Add a restrained faint cobalt interlocking-circle diaper in small reserved background areas, leaving generous antique-white breathing space. A narrow ruyi-lappet rhythm immediately inside the floral perimeter may connect the zones, but retain the same overall border width as the reference. Sophisticated porcelain drawing, exquisite rhythm, clear hierarchy, blossoms have structural contours and subtle underglaze-like interior strokes, no airbrushed petals. This must look substantially different from a Western scrolling floral card. One complete single back artwork.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this single flat playing card back. Retain exactly its antique-white ground, palette, fine rendering, narrow outer margin, outer floral border width and shape, rounded corners, four smaller diagonal floral roundels, and overall 5:7 proportions. Make ONE compositional correction: remove the large pointed central cartouche and ALL enclosed motifs and replace it with a much smaller perfectly CIRCULAR Tang-inspired composite treasure-flower medallion, no more than 29 percent of total card width. The round medallion should be a genuinely eightfold radially symmetric abstraction: eight identical fan-petal lobes surrounding a tiny circular flower center, repeated evenly like a silk brocade flower viewed face-on. It must have NO upright directional blossom, no stem, no top or bottom, no point at any of its four compass directions, no pointed shield, no quatrefoil silhouette, no Persian or Western cartouche. Reserve the newly freed area as antique-white breathing space and connect it naturally to existing slender lotus stems, with delicate interlocking-circle brocade tracery of low visual weight. Keep a balanced two-way playing-card composition. The central flower is a small jewel within the overall pattern, not a large badge. Flat full-frame single card image, no text, no scene, no shadow.
